title: Shape of Data Distributions
contentObjective: I can describe the shape of a data distribution as symmetric, skewed, or having clusters and gaps.
languageObjective: I can explain my description using the words symmetric, skewed, cluster, and gap.

noticeAndWonder.context: The team's data analyst pulls up two dot plots. Fan ages at last night's game: 18, 19, 20, 20, 21, 21, 22, 68 (one grandparent came too). Roster shoe sizes: 9, 10, 10, 10.5, 11, 11, 11.5. Look at where the values bunch up and where a tail stretches out in each plot. What do you notice about the shape of each data set, and what do you wonder about why one has a long tail and the other doesn't?
wonderStarters: I wonder what would happen if…

revealWordProblem.title: Apply: Rebounds in Last Night's Game
revealWordProblem.text: The analytics team logs rebounds grabbed by each of the team's 7 players in last night's game: 3, 4, 4, 5, 5, 5, and 16 (the starting center had a huge night on the boards). Describe the shape of this data set, calculate the mean and the median, and decide which measure of center best represents a 'typical' player's rebounds. Explain your reasoning.
revealWordProblem.sampleAnswer: The distribution is skewed right: six players cluster between 3 and 5 rebounds, while the center's 16 rebounds forms a long tail stretching to the right. Mean: (3 + 4 + 4 + 5 + 5 + 5 + 16) ÷ 7 = 42 ÷ 7 = 6. Median: arranging the 7 values in order (3, 4, 4, 5, 5, 5, 16), the middle (4th) value is 5. The median (5) is the better measure of a 'typical' player's rebounds because the mean (6) is pulled upward by the center's outlier game of 16 rebounds — a value no other player came close to.

launch.narrative: The league analyst is studying three different data sets from the season: (1) Player heights across all teams, (2) Number of 3-pointers per game by each player, and (3) Years of experience for all coaches. Each data set has a different shape when graphed. Your job is to describe each shape and explain what it tells us about the data.
launch.contextImage: Three different histogram shapes displayed on a sports analytics dashboard
noticePrompts: Do the three data sets look the same when graphed?
Which graph has data bunched in the middle? Which has a long tail?
Are there any gaps or clusters you can spot?
wonderPrompts: Why would different sports data have different shapes?
Does the shape tell you which measure of center to use?

conceptIntro.heading: What shape is the data?
conceptIntro.intro: The shape of a data distribution describes how the values are spread out. Data can be symmetric (the same on both sides), skewed (bunched on one side with a long tail on the other), or have clusters and gaps.
conceptIntro.keyIdea: Symmetric data mirrors around the center; skewed data has a long tail, and the skew is named for the direction the tail points.

iDo.title: Watch me
lines: Example 1, bar heights from left to right: 2, 5, 8, 5, 2. The bars rise to a peak in the middle and fall evenly on both sides.
Both sides look like mirror images, so this shape is symmetric.
Example 2, bar heights: 9, 6, 3, 1. The tallest bars are on the left and the bars get shorter going right.
The long tail points to the right, so this shape is skewed right. I name the skew after the tail, not the peak.

weDo.title: Let's try together
lines: New bar heights: 1, 3, 6, 9. Where are the tallest bars, and which way does the tail point?
Since the tail points left, is this symmetric, skewed right, or skewed left?
Now picture heights 2, 6, 6, 2. Do both sides match? What shape is that?

youDo.title: Now it's your turn
lines: Next, you will match each sports data description to its shape: symmetric, skewed right, or skewed left.
Look for the long tail to decide the direction of the skew.

explore.label: Match each sports data description with the shape of its distribution.

cards.text: Player heights: most players are around 5'8"–5'10", with equal numbers taller and shorter
3-pointers per game: most players make 0–2, a few make 3–5, and rarely anyone makes 6+
Free-throw percentage for experienced players: most shoot 70%–90%, a few shoot below 50%
100-meter dash times: most runners are around 12–13 seconds, equal numbers faster and slower
Career home runs: most players hit fewer than 100, a few superstars hit 400+
Senior athletes' reaction times: most are fast (0.2–0.3s), a few are very slow (0.6s+)

discourse.prompt: When data is skewed right, is the mean or median a better measure of center? Why?
discourse.sentenceFrame: When data is skewed right, the tail pulls the ___ toward the ___. The ___ is a better measure because it is not affected by ___. For symmetric data, the mean and median are ___.

optional.stem: A histogram has a long tail of high values stretching to the right. What is its shape?
optional.explanation: A tail of high values stretching to the right means the distribution is skewed right. The skew is named for the tail's direction.
choiceFeedback: Each dot represents one occurrence—count all the dots.
One dot at 2, three dots at 5—add them.
Total dots = total data points.
optional.stemEs: Un histograma tiene una cola larga de valores altos que se extiende hacia la derecha. ¿Cuál es su forma?
optional.explanationEs: Una cola de valores altos que se extiende hacia la derecha significa que la distribución está sesgada a la derecha. El sesgo se nombra por la dirección de la cola.
hints: Skew is always named for the direction the long tail stretches, not for the side with the tall bars.
Find the tail first, then decide left or right from where it points.
The tail here stretches toward the higher values on the right side of the display — use that direction to name the shape.
hintsEs: El sesgo siempre se nombra por la dirección hacia la que se extiende la cola larga, no por el lado con las barras altas.
Primero halla la cola y luego decide izquierda o derecha según hacia dónde apunta.
Aquí la cola se extiende hacia los valores más altos, en el lado derecho de la gráfica: usa esa dirección para nombrar la forma.
choicesEs: Sesgada a la derecha
Sesgada a la izquierda
Simétrica
Uniforme

optional.stem: A dot plot has one peak in the middle and even sides. What shape is it?
choices: Symmetric with one cluster around the peak
optional.explanation: One peak in the middle with roughly even sides means the data mirrors around the center, so it is symmetric with a single cluster at the peak.
choiceFeedback: Dots stack vertically—count all dots in the plot.
If a score has no dots, it wasn't observed.
Total dots = total quiz attempts.
optional.stemEs: Un diagrama de puntos tiene un solo pico en el centro y lados parejos. ¿Qué forma tiene?
optional.explanationEs: Un solo pico en el centro con lados aproximadamente parejos significa que los datos se reflejan alrededor del centro, así que es simétrica con un solo grupo en el pico.
hints: A cluster is a group of data values bunched together, and symmetric means the two sides mirror each other.
Check whether one side has a long tail that the other side lacks — that would rule symmetry out.
Compare the left side of the peak with the right side, then decide which shape word fits what you see.
hintsEs: Un grupo es un conjunto de datos que se acumulan juntos, y simétrica significa que los dos lados se reflejan entre sí.
Revisa si un lado tiene una cola larga que el otro no tiene: eso descartaría la simetría.
Compara el lado izquierdo del pico con el derecho y luego decide qué palabra de forma corresponde a lo que ves.
choicesEs: Simétrica con un grupo alrededor del pico
Sesgada a la derecha
Sesgada a la izquierda
Tiene un espacio grande

optional.instructions: Sort each described sports display into the shape feature it shows best.

items.text: Goals per game: one peak at 1 goal, an even rise and fall on both sides
Coach experience (years): most coaches at 1-5 years, a long tail out to 30+ years
Veteran kickers' field-goal %: most near 90%, a long tail down to a few near 40%
Race times: a group at 12s, nothing from 13-19s, then a group at 20s
Jersey numbers: most players bunched tightly between 20 and 29

optional.explanation: Each description names its own giveaway feature. One peak with an even rise and fall on both sides is symmetric. Coach experience piles up at 1–5 years with a long stretch out to 30+, a tail pointing right. Kickers near 90% with a few down at 40% have a tail pointing left. Race times with nothing at all from 13–19 seconds show a gap, and jersey numbers packed between 20 and 29 show a cluster.
optional.explanationEs: Cada descripción menciona la característica que la delata. Un solo pico que sube y baja de forma pareja a ambos lados es simétrico. La experiencia de los entrenadores se acumula entre 1 y 5 años con un tramo largo hasta más de 30, una cola que apunta a la derecha. Los pateadores cerca del 90% con unos pocos en 40% tienen una cola que apunta a la izquierda. Los tiempos de carrera sin ningún dato entre 13 y 19 segundos muestran un espacio vacío, y los números de camiseta apretados entre 20 y 29 muestran una agrupación.
hints: Five different features are in play: symmetry, two skew directions, a gap, and a cluster. Read each description for the one detail that gives it away.
Ask three questions per card: does the data mirror itself around a center, does a long tail stretch one direction, or is there an empty stretch or a tight bunch?
Try the race times card: there is a group at 12s and another at 20s with nothing from 13 to 19. Decide what that empty stretch is called, then work through the rest.
hintsEs: Hay cinco características en juego: la simetría, las dos direcciones de sesgo, un espacio vacío y una agrupación. Lee cada descripción buscando el detalle que la delata.
Hazte tres preguntas por tarjeta: ¿los datos se reflejan alrededor de un centro?, ¿hay una cola larga que se estira hacia un lado?, ¿o hay un tramo vacío o un grupo muy apretado?
Prueba con la tarjeta de los tiempos de carrera: hay un grupo en 12 s y otro en 20 s, sin nada entre 13 y 19. Decide cómo se llama ese tramo vacío y luego sigue con las demás.
optional.instructionsEs: Clasifica cada representación deportiva descrita según la característica de forma que muestra mejor.

optional.label: Display 4: Match each feature you spot in a data display to the term that names it.

pairs.term: The tallest point of the display where data piles up
An empty interval with no data values between two groups
A group of values bunched close together
A long stretch of low bars trailing off to one side

optional.explanation: Each description names one feature of a data display: the tallest pile-up point is the peak, an empty interval between two groups is a gap, values bunched close together form a cluster, and a long stretch of low bars trailing off to one side is the tail. The tail is the feature that names the direction of a skew.
optional.explanationEs: Cada descripción nombra una característica de una representación de datos: el punto más alto donde se acumulan los datos es el pico, un intervalo vacío entre dos grupos es un espacio vacío, los valores muy juntos forman una agrupación, y un tramo largo de barras bajas que se aleja hacia un lado es la cola. La cola es la característica que nombra la dirección del sesgo.
hints: These four words describe what you SEE in a display: where data piles up, where it is missing, where it bunches together, and where it trails off.
Sort by what each description is about — height (the highest point), emptiness (nothing there), closeness (bunched together), or trailing off to one side.
Start with "an empty interval with no data values between two groups." The word "empty" points to the term for a hole in the data. Then match the other three.
hintsEs: Estas cuatro palabras describen lo que VES en una representación: dónde se acumulan los datos, dónde faltan, dónde se juntan y hacia dónde se alejan.
Clasifica según de qué habla cada descripción: altura (el punto más alto), vacío (no hay nada ahí), cercanía (muy juntos) o alejamiento hacia un lado.
Empieza con "un intervalo vacío sin valores entre dos grupos". La palabra "vacío" apunta al término que nombra un hueco en los datos. Luego empareja los otros tres.
optional.labelEs: Representación 4: Une cada característica que detectes en una representación de datos con el término que la nombra.

optional.stem: A histogram: most players are at 70-85%, a gap sits at 50-65%, and a few are at 40-50%. Name the shape and features.
choices: A cluster (70-85%), a gap (50-65%), and a left tail — so skewed left
A symmetric display with no gaps
A right tail of high values — so skewed right
Two equal peaks with no cluster or gap
optional.explanation: The data clusters at the high end (70-85%), there is an empty gap (50-65%), and the few low values form a tail on the left, so the display is skewed left.
choiceFeedback: No gaps and no tail here—but these are present.
This doesn't have equal halves—it's not symmetric.
The tail goes low (left)—that direction shows skew direction.
optional.stemEs: Un histograma: la mayoría de los jugadores está en 70-85%, hay una brecha en 50-65% y unos pocos están en 40-50%. Nombra la forma y sus características.
optional.explanationEs: Los datos se agrupan en el extremo alto (70-85%), hay una brecha vacía (50-65%) y los pocos valores bajos forman una cola a la izquierda, así que la gráfica está sesgada a la izquierda.
hints: Three features can show up together: a cluster where data piles up, a gap where an interval is empty, and a tail where a few values trail off.
Locate the cluster and the gap first, then see which side the leftover values sit on — that side is the tail.
The bulk of the data sits at the high end and the few remaining values sit far below it. Decide which direction the tail runs, then name the skew after it.
hintsEs: Pueden aparecer tres características juntas: un grupo donde se acumulan los datos, una brecha donde un intervalo está vacío y una cola donde unos pocos valores se alejan.
Ubica primero el grupo y la brecha; luego observa de qué lado quedan los demás valores: ese lado es la cola.
La mayoría de los datos está en el extremo alto y los pocos valores restantes quedan muy por debajo. Decide hacia dónde va la cola y nombra el sesgo según esa dirección.
choicesEs: Un grupo (70-85%), un espacio (50-65%) y una cola a la izquierda — o sea, sesgada a la izquierda
Una representación simétrica sin espacios
Una cola de valores altos a la derecha — o sea, sesgada a la derecha
Dos picos iguales sin grupo ni espacio

optional.title: Level 2 Extension — Name the Skew by Its Tail

workedExample.label: Display
workedExample.work: Analytics screen: minutes played per game. Bar heights left to right: 12, 8, 4, 2, 1.

workedExample.label: Cluster
workedExample.work: Most players are bunched on the left (low minutes).

workedExample.label: Tail
workedExample.work: The short bars trail off toward the right (high minutes).

workedExample.label: Shape claim
workedExample.work: Because the tall bars (the peak) are on the LEFT, this display is left-skewed.

optional.correctWork: This display is skewed RIGHT, not left. Skew is named for the direction the TAIL points, not where the peak sits. The peak is on the left, but the long tail of short bars stretches to the right, so it is skewed right. (A correct claim-evidence-reasoning answer: 'The distribution is skewed right because I see the tail stretching toward the high values on the right.')
hints: Ask: which way does the long tail of short bars point, not where is the tallest bar?
The peak is on the left and the tail stretches right. Skew is named for the tail, so this is skewed right.
optional.titleEs: Extensión de Nivel 2: Nombra el sesgo por su cola
optional.explanation: The claim was based on where the peak sits instead of where the tail points. The bar heights 12, 8, 4, 2, 1 pile up on the left and shrink toward the right, so the tail stretches right and the display is skewed right. Skew is always named for the tail direction, never the peak.
optional.explanationEs: La afirmación se basó en dónde está el pico y no en hacia dónde apunta la cola. Las alturas de las barras 12, 8, 4, 2, 1 se acumulan a la izquierda y se reducen hacia la derecha, así que la cola se estira a la derecha y la representación está sesgada a la derecha. El sesgo siempre se nombra por la dirección de la cola, nunca por el pico.

approaching.stem: A histogram of basketball players' ages shows: most players are 22–28, with a long tail of older players up to age 40. What is the shape of this distribution?
approaching.explanation: Most data is on the left (younger ages) with a tail stretching right (older ages). This is skewed right.
choiceFeedback: Count dots at heights below your target height.
Dots above the line don't count—look at dots below.
Add dots at each height that's shorter.
hints: Locate the crowd and the tail: most players are 22–28 (the left side), with a thin tail stretching out to age 40 (the right side).
Skew is named after the TAIL — the direction the long thin end stretches — not after where the big cluster sits.
First step: sketch it — tall bars at ages 22–28, shrinking bars out to 40. Point your finger along the tail and name that direction.
approaching.stemEs: Un histograma de las edades de jugadores de baloncesto muestra que la mayoría tiene entre 22 y 28 años, con una cola larga de jugadores mayores hasta los 40 años. ¿Cuál es la forma de esta distribución?
approaching.explanationEs: La mayoría de los datos está a la izquierda (edades menores) y la cola se extiende hacia la derecha (edades mayores). Esto es sesgada a la derecha.
choicesEs: Sesgada a la derecha
Simétrica
Sesgada a la izquierda
Uniforme

approaching.stem: A data set is symmetric. What is likely true about the mean and median?
choices: The mean is much higher than the median
The median is much higher than the mean
They are always exactly the same
approaching.explanation: In a symmetric distribution, the mean and median are approximately equal because the data is balanced on both sides.
choiceFeedback: Count dots at scores below 80.
Dots at 80 or higher don't count.
Add up dots at all lower scores.
hints: Symmetric means the left and right sides mirror each other around the center — no long tail on either side.
A tail is what PULLS the mean away from the median. Ask: with no tail at all, how far apart could the two measures drift?
First step: test a symmetric set like 2, 4, 6, 8, 10 — find its mean and median and compare. Also watch for the word 'always' in the choices.
approaching.stemEs: Un conjunto de datos es simétrico. ¿Qué es probable que sea cierto sobre la media y la mediana?
approaching.explanationEs: En una distribución simétrica, la media y la mediana son aproximadamente iguales porque los datos están equilibrados a ambos lados.
choicesEs: Son aproximadamente iguales
La media es mucho más alta que la mediana
La mediana es mucho más alta que la media
Siempre son exactamente iguales

approaching.stem: Match each description with the correct distribution shape.

pairs.left: Equal amounts of data on both sides of the center
Most data on the left, tail stretches right
Most data on the right, tail stretches left
Data values grouped tightly with nothing nearby

approaching.hint: Look at each dot plot—count where most dots cluster and where the tail goes.
hints: Four shape words: two skews, one balanced shape, and one about tight grouping. Read each description for tail direction or grouping.
Use the tail rule: a skew is named for the direction its tail stretches. Balanced sides mean symmetric; a tight group with space around it is different.
Start with 'Equal amounts of data on both sides of the center' — a perfectly balanced picture. Pair it, then use the tail rule for the skews.
approaching.stemEs: Empareja cada descripción con la forma de distribución correcta.
approaching.explanation: Each description points to where the bulk of the data sits and which way the tail stretches: a tail to the right means skewed right, a tail to the left means skewed left, and balanced sides mean symmetric.
approaching.explanationEs: Cada descripción indica dónde está la mayoría de los datos y hacia dónde se extiende la cola: una cola hacia la derecha significa sesgada a la derecha, una cola hacia la izquierda significa sesgada a la izquierda, y lados equilibrados significan simétrica.

approaching.stem: Which word describes the direction of the TAIL, not the peak?
choices: Skew — the direction of the long tail tells you the skew direction
Skew — the direction of the peak tells you the skew direction
Skew — the direction the median points
Skew — the direction of the mode
approaching.explanation: The skew direction is named after the TAIL. If the tail stretches to the right, it is skewed right, even though the peak is on the left.
choiceFeedback: Direction of tail tells skew—where does the long thin part go?
The peak's position doesn't define skew—the tail does.
Median location is helpful, but tail direction defines skew.
hints: All four choices start with 'Skew' — the difference is WHICH feature (tail, peak, median, or mode) names the direction.
Picture a skewed-right dot plot: its peak sits on the LEFT, yet we call it skewed RIGHT. Ask which feature must be doing the naming.
First step: since a right-skewed plot has its peak on the left, the peak can't set the name. Test tail, median, and mode against that same picture.
approaching.stemEs: ¿Cuál palabra describe la dirección de la COLA, no del pico?
approaching.explanationEs: La dirección del sesgo se nombra según la COLA. Si la cola se extiende hacia la derecha, está sesgada a la derecha, aunque el pico esté a la izquierda.
choicesEs: El sesgo — la dirección de la cola larga te dice la dirección del sesgo
El sesgo — la dirección del pico te dice la dirección del sesgo
El sesgo — la dirección hacia donde apunta la mediana
El sesgo — la dirección de la moda

approaching.instructions: Sort each histogram description into its shape.
hints: Symmetric: bars rise and fall evenly from the center. The pattern mirrors itself.
Skewed right: tallest bars on the left, trailing off to the right. Skewed left: opposite.
approaching.label: Sort each bar pattern into the correct distribution shape.
approaching.explanation: Read the bar heights from left to right. 2, 5, 8, 5, 2 and 3, 6, 6, 3 mirror themselves around the middle, so they are symmetric. 8, 5, 3, 1 and 10, 6, 2, 1, 1 start tall and shrink toward the right, so their tails point right — skewed right. 1, 3, 5, 8 and 1, 1, 2, 6, 10 do the opposite, with the tail stretching left.
approaching.explanationEs: Lee las alturas de las barras de izquierda a derecha. 2, 5, 8, 5, 2 y 3, 6, 6, 3 se reflejan alrededor del centro, así que son simétricas. 8, 5, 3, 1 y 10, 6, 2, 1, 1 empiezan altas y se reducen hacia la derecha, así que sus colas apuntan a la derecha: sesgadas a la derecha. 1, 3, 5, 8 y 1, 1, 2, 6, 10 hacen lo contrario, con la cola extendiéndose hacia la izquierda.
approaching.labelEs: Clasifica cada patrón de barras en la forma de distribución correcta.

approaching.title: Spot the Common Mistake

workedExample.label: Data
workedExample.work: Goals per game dot plot — 0: 8 dots, 1: 6 dots, 2: 3 dots, 3: 1 dot, 4: 1 dot.

workedExample.label: Look
workedExample.work: The tallest stacks of dots are on the LEFT (0 and 1 goals); the dots trail off to the right toward 4 goals.

workedExample.label: Shape claim
workedExample.work: The tallest bars are on the left, so the student calls this distribution skewed LEFT.

approaching.correctWork: This distribution is skewed RIGHT, not left. The student named the skew after where the peak sits, but skew is named for the direction the TAIL points. The peak (tallest stacks) is on the left at 0–1 goals, and the tail of short stacks stretches to the right toward 4. A tail pointing right means skewed right.
hints: Don't name the skew after the tallest bar — name it after the long tail.
The dots pile up at 0–1 and trail off toward 4. The tail points right, so the shape is skewed right.
approaching.explanation: The shape was named after the peak instead of the tail. The dots pile up on the left at 0 and 1 goal, and the short stacks stretch out to the right toward 4 goals. Skew is named for the direction the tail points, so this distribution is skewed right.
approaching.explanationEs: La forma se nombró por el pico en lugar de por la cola. Los puntos se acumulan a la izquierda, en 0 y 1 gol, y las pilas cortas se extienden hacia la derecha, hacia los 4 goles. El sesgo se nombra por la dirección a la que apunta la cola, así que esta distribución está sesgada a la derecha.

onLevel.stem: A dot plot of goals scored per game shows: 0(5 dots), 1(7 dots), 2(4 dots), 3(2 dots), 4(1 dot). What is the shape?
choices: Skewed right — most values at the low end with a tail to the right
Skewed left — most values at the high end
Uniform — all bars the same height
onLevel.explanation: The data peaks at 0–1 goals and tails off toward 4. Most data is on the left with fewer values stretching right — this is skewed right.
choiceFeedback: Clusters mean dots are close together at certain values.
Spread means dots are scattered across a wide range.
Look at how dots are grouped or spread out.
hints: Read the dot counts: 0 goals has 5 dots, 1 has 7, 2 has 4, 3 has 2, 4 has 1. Find where dots pile up and where they thin out.
The peak is at 1 goal, and the counts shrink as goals increase. Skew is named for the direction of that shrinking tail.
First step: sketch the dots as bars — 5, 7, 4, 2, 1 from left to right. Trace the falling heights toward 4 goals, then name that direction.
onLevel.stemEs: Un diagrama de puntos de goles anotados por partido muestra: 0 (5 puntos), 1 (7 puntos), 2 (4 puntos), 3 (2 puntos), 4 (1 punto). ¿Cuál es la forma?
onLevel.explanationEs: Los datos alcanzan su punto más alto en 0–1 goles y disminuyen hacia el 4. La mayoría de los datos está a la izquierda y unos pocos valores se extienden hacia la derecha: esto es sesgada a la derecha.
choicesEs: Sesgada a la derecha — la mayoría de los valores en el extremo bajo con una cola hacia la derecha
Simétrica — igual en los dos lados
Sesgada a la izquierda — la mayoría de los valores en el extremo alto
Uniforme — todas las barras de la misma altura

onLevel.label: Match each distribution shape to how its mean and median compare.

pairs.match: Mean ≈ Median — use either (mean is fine)
Mean > Median — use the median (high tail pulls the mean up)
Mean < Median — use the median (low tail pulls the mean down)

hints: Remember: a tail PULLS the mean toward itself, while the median barely moves. That one idea sorts all three cards.
Work each case: a high-value tail (right) drags the mean UP past the median; a low-value tail (left) drags it DOWN below. No tail = they match.
Start with Symmetric — no tail, so the mean and median sit together. Pair it with the '≈' card, then use tail direction for the other two.
onLevel.explanation: A tail pulls the mean toward it while the median barely moves, and that single idea sorts all three cards. Symmetric data has no tail, so the mean and median land together and either one works. Skewed right has high values in the tail that pull the mean above the median, and skewed left has low values that pull it below — in both skewed cases the median describes a typical value better.
onLevel.explanationEs: Una cola jala la media hacia ella mientras la mediana casi no se mueve, y esa sola idea ordena las tres tarjetas. Los datos simétricos no tienen cola, así que la media y la mediana quedan juntas y cualquiera de las dos sirve. El sesgo a la derecha tiene valores altos en la cola que jalan la media por encima de la mediana, y el sesgo a la izquierda tiene valores bajos que la jalan por debajo; en los dos casos sesgados la mediana describe mejor un valor típico.
onLevel.labelEs: Une cada forma de distribución con la comparación entre su media y su mediana.

onLevel.stem: Match the data shape with the best measure of center.

pairs.left: Data with a large gap and cluster

onLevel.hint: Ask: is the data clustered on one end with a tail, or roughly balanced?
hints: One question decides every card: could a tail, outlier, or gap drag the mean away from what's typical for the data?
Rule: balanced data → the mean is safe. Any skew, gap, or lopsided tail → the median resists the pull and stays near typical.
Start with 'Symmetric distribution': nothing pulls the mean there, so pair it with the Mean card. Ask which pull affects each of the other three.
onLevel.stemEs: Empareja la forma de los datos con la mejor medida de tendencia central.
onLevel.explanation: Shape decides which center is more trustworthy: in a symmetric distribution the mean and median agree, while a skewed one pulls the mean toward the tail, so the median stays closer to a typical value.
onLevel.explanationEs: La forma determina cuál medida de centro es más confiable: en una distribución simétrica la media y la mediana coinciden, mientras que en una sesgada la media se desplaza hacia la cola, así que la mediana queda más cerca de un valor típico.

onLevel.instructions: For each data set, decide: is it symmetric, skewed right, or skewed left?
hints: Look for outliers or tails. A high outlier creates a right skew. A low outlier creates a left skew.
If data is roughly even on both sides of the center, it is symmetric.
onLevel.label: Classify each data set by its distribution shape.
onLevel.explanation: Look for values that stretch far from the rest. The test scores 70, 75, 80, 80, 85, 90 spread evenly around the middle, so they are symmetric. The donations run $5 to $15 and then jump to $200, a high value that stretches the tail right. The quiz scores cluster from 75 to 95 with a single 30 far below, so that tail stretches left.
onLevel.explanationEs: Busca los valores que se alejan mucho del resto. Las calificaciones 70, 75, 80, 80, 85, 90 se reparten de forma pareja alrededor del centro, así que son simétricas. Las donaciones van de $5 a $15 y luego saltan a $200, un valor alto que estira la cola hacia la derecha. Las notas del examen se agrupan entre 75 y 95 con un solo 30 muy por debajo, así que esa cola se estira hacia la izquierda.
onLevel.labelEs: Clasifica cada conjunto de datos según la forma de su distribución.

onLevel.title: Spot the Common Mistake

workedExample.label: Shape
workedExample.work: Most salaries cluster at 1–3 million with one value way out at 40 million, so the distribution is skewed right. ✓

workedExample.label: Best measure
workedExample.work: The student picks the MEAN to describe a typical salary because the shape is skewed right.

onLevel.correctWork: The shape is correct (skewed right), but the MEDIAN — not the mean — is the better measure for skewed data. The single 40-million salary is an extreme value in the right tail that pulls the mean up to about 6.75 million, far above what most players earn. The median is 2 million, which truly represents a typical salary. Use the median whenever data is skewed.
hints: The shape call is right — check the measure-of-center choice instead.
That one 40-million salary drags the mean up to ~6.75 while the median stays at 2. For skewed data, use the median.
onLevel.explanation: The shape call was correct, but the measure of center was not. The single 40-million salary sits far out in the right tail and drags the mean up to about 6.75 million, higher than every other player actually earns. The median of 2 million truly describes a typical salary, so skewed data should be summarized with the median.
onLevel.explanationEs: La forma estaba bien identificada, pero la medida de centro no. El único salario de 40 millones queda muy lejos, en la cola derecha, y arrastra la media hasta unos 6.75 millones, más de lo que gana cualquier otro jugador. La mediana de 2 millones sí describe un salario típico, así que los datos sesgados se deben resumir con la mediana.

extending.title: Find the Shape Error

workedExample.label: Shape
workedExample.work: Skewed left because the tall bar is on the right side

workedExample.label: Best measure
workedExample.work: Use the mean because skewed data uses the mean

extending.correctWork: This is skewed RIGHT, not left. The cluster of data is on the left (10–11 seconds) and the tail with the extreme value (14.8) stretches to the right. Also, for skewed data the MEDIAN is the better measure, not the mean, because the mean is pulled toward the tail.
hints: The direction of the skew is the direction of the TAIL, not the peak. Where is the long tail?
The peak is on the left (10–11 seconds) and the tail stretches right to 14.8. That means skewed RIGHT.
extending.explanation: The shape was named from the tall bar instead of the tail. The histogram clusters at 10–11 seconds, shows empty intervals at 12 and 13, and then has one lone value at 14.8, so the stretched-out tail points right — skewed right. And because the data is skewed, the median describes a typical sprint time better than the mean, which the 14.8 pulls upward.
extending.explanationEs: La forma se nombró por la barra alta en lugar de por la cola. El histograma se agrupa entre 10 y 11 segundos, muestra intervalos vacíos en 12 y 13, y luego tiene un solo valor en 14.8, así que la cola alargada apunta a la derecha: sesgada a la derecha. Y como los datos están sesgados, la mediana describe mejor un tiempo típico que la media, a la que el 14.8 jala hacia arriba.

extending.prompt: A teacher shows two dot plots of quiz scores from two different classes. Class A's data is symmetric with a cluster around 80. Class B's data is skewed right with most scores between 60–70 and a few scores near 100. Compare the classes: which has a higher median? Which has a higher mean? In which class does the mean better represent a typical score?
extending.sentenceFrame: Class A is ___ with scores clustered around ___. Class B is skewed ___ with most scores at ___. Class A likely has a ___ median. Class B's mean is pulled ___ by the high scores. The mean better represents a typical score in Class ___ because ___.
extending.hint: Start by describing each dot plot's shape: cluster, gap, or tail—then compare consistency.
hints: Class A: symmetric around 80. Class B: most scores 60–70 with a few near 100 — that's a right tail. Note both shapes before comparing.
Plan: medians come from where MOST scores sit (near 80 vs the 60s). For means, ask what Class B's few 100s do. Then decide where mean = typical.
Start with the medians: Class A's middle score sits near its 80 cluster; Class B's sits in the 60–70 pile. Compare those, then tackle the means.
extending.explanation: Class A's scores center on 80 while most of Class B's sit between 60 and 70, so Class A has the higher median and the higher mean. Class B's few scores near 100 pull its mean up above its 60s cluster, but not past Class A. The mean represents a typical score better in Class A, because a symmetric distribution has no tail tugging the mean away from the center — Class B is skewed right, so its median is the fairer summary.
extending.explanationEs: Las notas de la Clase A se centran en 80, mientras que la mayoría de las de la Clase B están entre 60 y 70, así que la Clase A tiene la mediana y la media más altas. Las pocas notas cercanas a 100 de la Clase B jalan su media por encima de su grupo de los 60, pero no más allá de la Clase A. La media representa mejor una nota típica en la Clase A, porque una distribución simétrica no tiene una cola que jale la media lejos del centro; la Clase B está sesgada a la derecha, así que su mediana es el mejor resumen.
extending.promptEs: Un maestro muestra dos diagramas de puntos con los puntajes de dos grupos distintos. Los datos del grupo A son simétricos con un grupo alrededor de 80. Los datos del grupo B están sesgados a la derecha, con la mayoría de los puntajes entre 60 y 70 y algunos cerca de 100. Compara los grupos: ¿cuál tiene la mediana más alta? ¿Cuál tiene la media más alta? ¿En cuál grupo representa mejor la media un puntaje típico?

extending.instructions: Drag each real-world data set under the distribution shape it would most likely form.

categories.label: Skewed Left
items: An experienced archer's scores out of 100

hints: Symmetric: most values cluster in the middle with equal tails on both sides.
Skewed RIGHT: a few very HIGH values (e.g., superstar earnings) stretch the tail right.
Skewed LEFT: a few very LOW values (e.g., a few bad rounds) stretch the tail left.
extending.label: Sort each data set by its likely histogram shape.
extending.explanation: Match each context to what its values would do. Player heights bunch near an average with about as many taller as shorter players, so that histogram is symmetric. Career earnings include a few superstars far above everyone else, and those high values stretch the tail right. An experienced archer scores near 100 most rounds with only a few low rounds, and those low values stretch the tail left.
extending.explanationEs: Relaciona cada situación con lo que harían sus valores. Las estaturas de los jugadores se agrupan cerca de un promedio, con casi tantos más altos como más bajos, así que ese histograma es simétrico. Las ganancias de carrera incluyen a unas pocas estrellas muy por encima del resto, y esos valores altos estiran la cola hacia la derecha. Un arquero con experiencia anota cerca de 100 en casi todas las rondas y solo tiene unas pocas rondas bajas, y esos valores bajos estiran la cola hacia la izquierda.
extending.labelEs: Clasifica cada conjunto de datos según la forma probable de su histograma.

optionalActivity.name: Distribution Shape Gallery Walk
optionalActivity.intro: Walk the league's analytics gallery and name the shape of each sports data display you see.

practice.commonMistake: A common mistake in Shape of Data Distributions is naming the skew by looking at where the TALLEST bar (the peak) sits, instead of looking at which way the TAIL stretches. For example, given bar heights 8, 5, 3, 1 (tall on the left, trailing off to the right), students often say "skewed left" because the peak is on the left — but the correct name is skewed right, because skew is always named for the direction the tail points, not the peak.

diagram.title: Marathon Finish Times — Histogram
diagram.caption: The peak sits between 3.5 and 4.5 hours, then a long right tail stretches out to 7 — a right-skewed distribution.

connect.scenario: A sports reporter is writing about marathon finish times. The histogram below shows the data: most runners finish between 3.5–4.5 hours, and a long tail of slower runners stretches out to 5–7 hours.

visual.title: Marathon finish times
visual.caption: Runners pile up around 3.5–4.5 hours; a long tail of slower finishers stretches RIGHT toward 7 hours (skewed right).

connect.promptQuestion: What is the shape of this distribution? Should the reporter use the mean or median to describe a 'typical' finish time?
connect.prompt: The distribution is skewed ___ because the tail stretches toward the ___ finish times. There is a cluster around ___. The reporter should use the ___ because the ___ would be pulled toward the ___ by the extreme values.

exitTicket.stem: A data set has most values clustered between 40–60, with a few values at 90–100. What is the shape of the distribution and which measure of center is best?
exitTicket.explanation: The data clusters on the left (40–60) with a tail to the right (90–100). This is skewed right. The median is best because the mean would be pulled toward the high values.
choiceFeedback: A few high values create a tail — the data isn't symmetric.
The tail points toward the HIGH values, so it's skewed right.
The values aren't evenly spread — there's a cluster and a tail.
hints: Sketch it: a big pile of values at 40–60 and a few far away at 90–100. That cluster-and-tail picture is your shape clue.
Two decisions: (1) does the tail point toward the HIGH end or the LOW end? (2) with a tail, which center measure resists being pulled? Match both.
First step: the few values at 90–100 sit ABOVE the cluster — decide the tail's direction from that, then pick the measure a tail can't drag.

questions.stem: In a histogram, what does the height of each bar represent?
choices: The frequency (count) of data in that interval
The average of the data in that interval
questions.explanation: Each bar's height shows the frequency — how many data values fall within that interval.

questions.stem: A histogram bar for the interval 20–29 reaches a height of 7. What does the 7 tell you?
questions.explanation: A bar's height is the frequency — here, 7 values land in the 20–29 interval.

questions.stem: A histogram has intervals: 0–4, 5–9, 10–14, 15–19. What is the width of each interval?
questions.explanation: Each interval covers 5 values (0,1,2,3,4 then 5,6,7,8,9 etc.), so the width is 5.
